stories.title: US and Canadian stocks tumble into correction after AI‑driven sell‑off
stories.summary: A sharp tech‑driven sell‑off on Friday pushed the Nasdaq Composite down 1,225.05 points (‑5.13%) to 22,654.15, erasing all gains recorded in 2026. The S&P 500 fell 257.38 points (‑3.59%) to 6,918.45 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 908.88 points (‑1.85%) to 48,188.18, moving both U.S. indices into correction territory. Canadian indices also slipped into correction as AI‑related concerns spread.
stories.why: The drop reflects heightened investor anxiety about AI profitability, which may reshape capital allocation in the technology sector.

stories.title: Trump says he will ban US firms from building AI data centres abroad
stories.summary: Donald Trump told reporters that U.S. companies will be barred from constructing AI data centres outside the United States and warned of a “tremendous tax” for firms that do so. He offered no details on how such a policy would be enforced or legislated. The comment came after his Asia trip, and follows data‑centre construction being a prominent issue in the recent midterm elections, with firms like Meta and Google already having overseas agreements.
stories.why: The proposal could significantly alter where major tech firms locate critical AI infrastructure and affect international investment decisions.

stories.title: Chips can survive the space environment
stories.summary: Even older chips retain value — according to Compute Credit Index Research , some H100s are selling for about half of their original cost basis from 2023, while some H200 configurations are selling for the same price they did when introduced in 2024. But you’re not going to repossess chips installed in a satellite orbiting 300 miles above Earth at 17,500 miles per hour.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.

stories.title: Russia hits Kyiv bridges and railway stations in overnight missile strike, nine killed
stories.summary: Russia launched an overnight ballistic missile attack that struck bridges in Kyiv and railway stations across Ukraine, occurring days after Ukraine damaged the Crimean Bridge; President Zelensky called it one of the war’s most massive strikes and the attacks killed at least nine people. The strikes coincided with diplomatic talks and followed President Putin’s warning of retaliation for the Crimean Bridge incident.
stories.why: The attacks target key transport infrastructure, disrupting civilian movement and influencing the war’s strategic and diplomatic dynamics.
